title: Prospective randomized study on the outcome after cemented vs. uncemented reverse total shoulder arthroplasty for proximal humerus fractures
summary:
Background:
Fractures of the upper arm near the shoulder are common, especially in older people. In many cases, treatment involves replacing the shoulder joint with an artificial implant. There are two different ways to fix the implant inside the bone: either using a special bone cement or without cement, allowing the implant to attach directly to the bone. It is still unclear which method leads to better results.

Research question:
The aim of this study is to compare these two fixation methods in terms of shoulder function, pain, quality of life, and possible complications.

Methods:
Patients with a fracture of the upper arm near the shoulder who require a shoulder replacement will be included in the study. The method used to fix the implant is assigned randomly. The surgery and follow-up treatment follow standard medical practice. After surgery, participants will be examined regularly over several months and years. These follow-up visits include assessments of movement, pain, quality of life, and possible complications.

interventions.name:

Patients with proximal humerus fractures receive a reverse total shoulder arthroplasty with uncemented (press-fit) humeral stem fixation following randomization as part of standard surgical care. This arm represents the control group.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Proximal humeral fracture with an indication for implantation of a reverse total shoulder arthroplasty, in which—based on the fracture configuration—both cemented and uncemented fixation are feasible
Age ≥ 18 years
Signed informed consent form
Exclusion criteria:
Minor age (< 18 years)
Lack of capacity to give informed consent
Pathological fracture
Prior surgeries or pre-existing pathologies of the affected shoulder
